title: AI Automation for EOB Processing: Tools & Workflows (2026)
summary: Learn how to automate EOB processing with Skyvern: retrieve payment documents, extract details, match claims, and post approved payments.
body_markdown:
If you're looking into EOB processing, there's probably someone on your team spending hours downloading insurance payment documents and copying the numbers into billing software. They log in to one insurer's website, find the right document, save it, and move on to the next.


We've built Skyvern for this kind of healthcare admin work. It's an[AI browser agent](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/what-is-browser-automation/) that can log into these websites, find the documents, and download them for you. You can build the rest of the workflow in Skyvern too, from extracting payment details to entering approved amounts in your billing portal.


Let me walk you through what EOB processing involves and how to get started with it in Skyvern.


## What is Explanation of Benefits (EOB) in Medical Billing?


An explanation of benefits (EOB) shows how an insurer handled a claim: what was billed, what insurance paid, and what the patient may owe. It isn’t a bill. Patients receive an EOB, while providers receive a payment explanation called a **remittance advice** .


EOB processing means using those payment details to update billing records. Your team matches the payment to the right claim, records the amounts, and checks for errors or missing payments.


For example, your practice bills $200, but its agreement with the insurer allows $150. If insurance pays $120 and assigns $30 to the patient, your team records those amounts and the $50 contractual adjustment. Codes on the document explain why amounts were adjusted or denied.


An **electronic remittance advice (ERA)** provides the same payment information in a standard file called X12 835, which billing software can read. This reduces manual entry, while your team reviews anything that doesn’t match.


## Benefits of Automating EOB Processing with AI


EOB automation collects payment documents, extracts the details, and passes checked data to your billing system. Your team reviews anything that needs attention.


This can help you:


- Reduce the time and cost of manual data entry.
- Update accounts sooner so staff can see what’s been paid.
- Catch denied claims and underpayments earlier.
- Give billers more time to investigate unclear documents and payment differences.


CAQH’s 2024 Index puts provider labor costs at $5.67 per manual remittance versus $2.95 electronically, based on 2023 data. These figures exclude software costs, so your savings will depend on setup costs and how much manual review is still needed.


## Key Steps in EOB Processing AI Automation


Let’s walk through how to build an EOB processing workflow in Skyvern, from collecting payment documents to recording approved payments. These five steps cover how to retrieve the files, extract payment details, match them to claims, and send anything that needs a closer look to your team.


### Step 1: Retrieval


Start by working out where your documents come from. ERAs may arrive through a clearinghouse, a service that passes claims and payment information between your practice and insurers. Your billing software may already receive files through one.


Paper checks and their payment explanations might arrive at your office or go to a medical lockbox service. That's a service that receives mailed payments, scans the checks and documents, and makes those images available to your team. CommerceHealthcare offers this kind of intake, for example.


For documents kept on an insurer's website, Skyvern can open the browser, log in, and download them for you. Give it the portal address, save your login credentials, and tell it which practice and payment dates to look for.


You'll need to set up two-factor authentication, or 2FA, too. That's the extra check after your password, such as a code from an authenticator app. Skyvern has[native 2FA support](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/credentials#authenticator-app) , including generating and entering authenticator codes automatically once you've saved the setup key.


For sites that send codes by email or text, you need a way to deliver those codes to Skyvern. You can enter them yourself or connect a service that forwards them to Skyvern.


Choose how the payer portal sends its authentication codes.


Set your workflow to download the records you need regularly and save them in your own approved storage. That way, you can still find an older payment explanation after it disappears from the portal's available history.


### Step 2: Intake and Classification


Once the files arrive, ask Skyvern to identify the insurer and document type as it reads each one. Give it categories such as payment explanation, denial letter, and scanned check so you can handle each one differently.


A single payment can cover several claims. Tell Skyvern to return a separate record for each claim and include the original document and payment reference with it.


You might receive an ERA and later download a PDF explaining the same payment. CAQH flags this as a source of duplicate posting. Add a check against previously processed payment references so your workflow recognizes them as two records of one payment.


### Step 3: Extraction


Next, pull the details out of each document. Skyvern can extract fields from a portal page or read downloaded PDFs and scanned images using its[file parser](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/reference/blocks#file-parser) .


For scanned documents, optical character recognition, or OCR, turns the text in the image into text software can read. AI then identifies which numbers belong to which fields.


Tell Skyvern exactly what you need: the claim number, service date, billed amount, allowed amount, insurer payment, patient share, and adjustment codes. Keep each service's details together when a claim includes several services.


The File Parser block accepts a file URL and a schema for the fields you want to extract.


If a scan is blurry or an amount is missing, send it to a person for review. Keep the original document beside the extracted fields so they can check the result without searching for it again.


### Step 4: Matching and Reconciliation


Skyvern can look up each claim in your billing portal using the claim number. Tell it to check supporting details, such as the patient and service date, before assigning the payment.


Give the workflow your payment records too, so it has the amounts you received to compare against. Add a[calculation step in Skyvern](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/reference/blocks#code) to check the totals using your team's rules.


CMS's Medicare remittance guidance explains that totals need to balance at the service, claim, and provider levels.


Sometimes the insurer has adjusted the overall payment, for example to recover an earlier overpayment. Your workflow needs to account for those adjustments before deciding that money is missing.


If it can't explain a difference, send the record for review before posting it.


### Step 5: Posting and Exceptions


Once a payment passes your checks, record it in your practice management system, the software your team uses to manage patient accounts and billing. If that system runs in a browser, Skyvern can enter the approved payment details into its forms.


You can configure Skyvern to[pause and request human input](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/reference/blocks#human-interaction) when a record needs review. Give the reviewer the claim, the source document, and a clear reason, such as "No matching claim found."


When you're getting started, review the results before letting the workflow post automatically. Include denied claims and documents with several claims in your trial so you can see how it handles more than straightforward payments.


Implementation time depends on how much of this is already connected. One portal with working credentials and an existing billing import needs less setup than several insurers with different formats. Test a complete batch through all five steps before estimating how long the rest will take.
